baseline_facts.content: Patient's name is Valerie Cole.

Patient has felt very anxious for about two months.
Patient dreads leaving the house every morning.
Patient dreads going to work.
Patient started a new job about two months ago.

Patient worries about her work performance.

Patient wakes before her alarm because of a racing heart.

Patient's palpitations feel irregular.
Patient's palpitations last from a couple of minutes to about ten minutes.
Patient has experienced palpitations for the past couple of months.
Patient once thought she was going to have a heart attack in the morning.
Patient reports pain when her heart is beating fast.
Patient reports no significant changes in appetite.
Patient eats regularly.
Patient eats more chocolate than normal.
Patient has very low energy during the daytime.
Patient finds no enjoyment in day-to-day activities.

Patient feels on edge all the time.

Patient finds it difficult to relax or see friends.
Patient sometimes avoids seeing friends.

Patient is not going out to run or play tennis as much.
Patient has not missed work due to symptoms.
Patient thinks about calling in sick most mornings.
Patient has not had a panic attack.
Public transport is very stressful for the patient.
Being on the tube is especially stressful for the patient.
Patient has not previously felt anxiety this bad.
Patient feels down and unhappy even at weekends.
Patient denies suicidal thoughts.
Patient has a good support system from family.
Patient lives with her parents.

Patient does not take drugs.

Doctor will provide online resources for anxiety management.

Doctor recommended basic blood tests to check for triggers of palpitations.
Doctor advised arranging a GP follow-up one week after blood tests.
Patient will call the support line to arrange blood tests.
Doctor did not suggest medication for anxiety initially.
Patient reports her symptoms have been getting worse over the past couple of months.
